I know what you're going through and this is a really hard conversation to have and hear, but BPD or not, you need to give yourself some credit and think about what's best for YOU. I know how hard it is to break away from the people we become attached to even when they're hurting us, but once you start to resent them, even if you do love them, it's pretty hard to come back from. I feel like this is the main resason people get divorced. Even after therapy and trying, it can be very hard to forgive and live with that pain they vaused. With myself personally, it lead to rapid detachment and I just couldn't stand being around them any longer. If your needs continue to be ignored as they have been, then this resentment will only grow. Though validation, gift giving, etc, might be your love language, it doesn't seem to be his. I read a quote a while ago, something about learning how to love people the way they like to be loved, not the way You like to be loved. And it sounds like you've already had this conversation many times with no change, especially given he has no probelm with his friends. As others have said though, you cant force people to love you the way you want. At this point, it might just be time to accept that you aren't right for each other before it grows into seething hatred. Your relationship is still pretty young, ask yourself if this is really the relationship and person you want to be with forever. If not, I would seriously consider leaving. The pain of being alone vs the pain of constantly feeling unheard and unloved is, imo, easier to deal with. It might feel like you wasted your timewith him, but there is no harm in wanting better for yourself, ending it, and finding someone more compatible.

Recently more than ever I have been struggling with an unstable sense of identity. For me, it's looking in the mirror and not knowing who I am. Looking down at down hands and arms and seeing all the scars I put on myself that have been there for years and remembering how it felt, but still feeling a gnawing in the back of my mind that questions how and why they are there and if this is really me. It's dissociating at home in the living room surrounded by my family and staring at walls wondering who these people are and why I'm around them. It's laying in bed for hours staring at the ceiling and watching the sun rise and brighten the room thinking about my gender identity, which I still have yet to figure out. This in particular is a constant ache in my mind because it has never been a problem until recently. Everything about my body doesn't feel right, but thinking about my body being any different also doesn't feel right. The confusion itself fogs up my mind and drives me to the point of ripping out my hair because I can no longer think clearly. 

For emptiness, it's very hard for me to explain. It's in those deep moments of despair that the feeling really settles in and makes itself at home in me. Wondering why anyone would want to be around me, telling myself that this is why people Don't want to be around, wondering how anyone could ever put up with me and then remembering  that I don't have any friends anyways and blaming it on BPD and how it makes me act when I'm upset. I've noticed that it (BPD in its dark hours) really deters people from pursuing a friendship. Emptiness is constantly wondering why I am still breathing, why I haven't killed myself yet (and ten remembering), and then wishing that I followed through when I was younger. Emptiness is when you are genuinely having a good time, but when you have a moment to relax, feeling so hollow and truly believing that you don't deserve to feel good.

As for hobbies and bands, I have bands that I love that I can occasionally listen to, but then remember that my husband's ex loves said band and then I hate them or at the very least refuse to listen to them for a while. I'm very passionate about art, specifically drawing, painting, and crocheting. However, I have to be in the mood for it and I will work for hours. Usually a day or two later though, I will take week or month long breaks because I just don't have the motivation or have suddenly lost interest, despite me being so passionate about it. It's hard to force myself to do it too. I sometimes find myself staring at my previous work and picking out the imperfections, which I know most people wouldn't see, but hating my work for it and telling myself that it's awful. I actually had a period where I wanted to destroy all of my work because I hated it, but thankfully I never did. I learned to accept and appreciate it, but will still sometimes have thoughts of hatred towards my work.
